newsitem.title: COSTA RICA: Costa Rica shelters Colombian guerrilla families.
newsitem.headline: Costa Rica shelters Colombian guerrilla families.

text.p: The Costa Rican government said on Thursday it had given political asylum to 20 relatives of members of Colombia's biggest Marxist guerrilla force, the Revolutionary Armed Forces of Colombia (FARC).

"They were given refugee status because the 20 Colombians alleged that their lives were in danger in Colombia because of their family link to FARC fighters," Security Ministry spokesman Hugo Solano told Reuters.

Solano said the Colombians had entered the country 15 days ago on International Red Cross passports with the government's permission. They were staying in private residences in the capital and in the nearby town of Heredia.

The FARC have been waging low-level war against the Colombian government since the early 1960s. With more than 10,000 fighters across the country, the group has ambushed and killed police, blown up key infrastructure and helped protect drug plantations and shipments.
Costa Rica's security police chief Mario Carpentier said the group included men, women and children, and had won support from the United Nations High Commission for Refugees.
The Costa Rican government has been attempting to act as a mediator in Colombia's guerrilla conflict.
Its negotiator, diplomat Guido Sibaja, has met government officials and guerrillas but has failed to make progress because of Colombia's awkward political situation.
President Ernesto Samper has been fighting for his political life after accusations that he knowingly took cocaine money for his 1994 election campaign -- a charge he denies.
